mainTopic: Does a נדה's backward impurity (מעת לעת) apply to תרומה or only to קודש? Testing רב הונא, and dough before and after kneading
overview: This amud keeps testing רב הונא's ruling about the 24-hour backward impurity (מעת לעת) of a נדה. First the גמרא explains the story of רבי: the הלכה had never been decided, but רבי remembered that many חכמים disagreed with רבי אליעזר, so he relied on him only בשעת הדחק. The גמרא argues the story must be about תרומה, since there was no קודש after the Temple. It answers, based on עולא, that some people still kept the purity standards of קודש. Two stories about רבן גמליאל's maidservants are also explained as קודש: the 'תרומה' loaves were the כהן's share of the לחמי תודה, set aside as dough, and the two questions came from two different maidservants. Then the גמרא brings another version, where רב הונא says מעת לעת applies to תרומה too. רב נחמן challenges him with a ברייתא, and רב שמואל בר רב יצחק explains that the ברייתא is about חולין kept at those purity levels. Finally the גמרא quotes a משנה from מסכת חלה: before kneading, dough is ordinary חולין and may be made impure, but after kneading it is treated like חלה and must be kept pure. A new ברייתא begins at the very end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What does 'after he remembered' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא and asks what רבי 'remembered.' It rejects the idea that he remembered the הלכה was against רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...in pressing circumstances.' And we discussed it: What does 'after he remembered' mean? If you say it means after he remembered that the הלכה is not like רבי אליעזר but like the רבנן, then how could he follow רבי אליעזר even in pressing circumstances?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the story of רבי and asks what exactly he 'remembered.' It tests one possible meaning and shows that it cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose רבי remembered that the הלכה was officially decided against רבי אליעזר. Then he could not rely on him at all, not even בשעת הדחק. So the word 'remembered' must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: In a pressing or difficult situation, when great need or loss is involved
And we discussed it (an earlier discussion that the גמרא is now bringing up)
If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
The final ruling of Jewish law

phrases.english: in pressing circumstances.
And we discussed it:
What does 'after he remembered' mean?
If you say: after he remembered
that the law is not like Rabbi Eliezer
but like the Rabbis,
then in pressing circumstances, how could he act like him?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָוֵינַן בַּהּ: מַאי ״לְאַחַר שֶׁנִּזְכַּר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted just before this passage, asking what one phrase in it means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What did רבי 'remember' that made him say רבי אליעזר may be relied on only בשעת הדחק?

steps.title: The law was undecided, but many disagreed with רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: No final הלכה had been stated. רבי remembered that a group, not one person, disagreed with רבי אליעזר, so he allowed relying on him only בשעת הדחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the הלכה had not been stated, neither like this חכם nor like that חכם. Once he remembered that it was not one person who disagreed with רבי אליעזר but many, he said: 'רבי אליעזר is worthy to rely on in pressing circumstances.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct meaning of 'after he remembered.' רבי realized that many חכמים disagreed with רבי אליעזר, even though no final ruling had been made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the הלכה follows the many against one person. Since no official ruling had been stated, רבי אליעזר's view was not ruled out. Still, because many disagreed, רבי limited relying on him to בשעת הדחק.

keyTerms.meaning: Neither like this master nor like that master; the matter was left undecided
A single חכם versus many חכמים; normally the הלכה follows the many
He is worthy of being relied upon

steps.whatToRemember: A minority opinion that was never officially rejected may be relied on בשעת הדחק.
steps.whyThisMatters: This story is a famous source for relying on a minority opinion in a time of great need, as long as the הלכה was never decided against it.

phrases.english: Rather, the law had not been stated,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets, 'לאו' ('is it not'). Either way, the meaning is the same.

phrases.english: neither like this master nor like that master,
phrases.notes: One 'master' is רבי אליעזר and the other is the רבנן.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵיוָן שֶׁנִּזְכַּר דְּלָאו יָחִיד פְּלִיג עֲלֵיהּ,
phrases.english: and once he remembered that it was not a single person who disagreed with him,
but many disagreed with him,
he said: 'Rabbi Eliezer is worthy'
to rely on in pressing circumstances.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא (לָאו) דְּלָא אִיתְּמַר הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1 with the correct meaning of 'remembered.'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The הלכה was undecided. רבי remembered that many disagreed with רבי אליעזר, so he allowed relying on him only בשעת הדחק.

steps.title: The case must have been תרומה, which seems to contradict רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that רבי's case must have involved תרומה, since there was no קודש in his time. That means the רבנן make her retroactively impure even for תרומה, against רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say the case was about תרומה, since there was תרומה in the days of רבי. But if you say it was about קודש, was there קודש in the days of רבי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now finishes its challenge against רב הונא. It points out that רבי's case could only have been about תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Temple was already destroyed in רבי's day, so there was no קודש to become impure. So the case was about תרומה, and the רבנן disagreed with רבי אליעזר even for תרומה. But רב הונא said that for תרומה even the רבנן agree she is impure only from the moment she sees blood.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well / granted (this option makes sense)
The portion of produce given to a כהן, which must be kept pure
Holy food from קרבנות, which has stricter purity rules

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether impurity rules existed in רבי's time. It is only whether actual קודש existed for the woman to touch after the Temple was destroyed.

phrases.english: It works well if you say it was about teruma,
that is fine, because there was teruma in the days of Rebbi,
but if you say it was about sacred food —
was there sacred food in the days of Rebbi?
phrases.notes: The Temple was already destroyed by then, so there were no קרבנות.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא לִתְרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the ברייתא now understood, the גמרא returns to using it as a challenge against רב הונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that for תרומה even the רבנן agree she is impure only from the moment she sees blood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The case must have been about תרומה, since there was no קודש in רבי's day. Since רבי relied on רבי אליעזר only בשעת הדחק, the רבנן must make her retroactively impure even for תרומה.

steps.title: Some people kept the purity standards of קודש even in רבי's time
steps.stepSummary: Based on עולא, some people still kept the purity standards of קודש in רבי's day. So the case could have been about קודש, and רב הונא stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like עולא said, for עולא said: The חברים purify their food in the גליל. Here too, in the days of רבי, people kept that standard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. In רבי's time, some people kept the purity standards of קודש, so the case could have been about קודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא reported that חברים in the גליל kept the purity standards of קודש even without a Temple. So רבי's case could have involved this level of purity. Then the dispute is only about קודש, exactly as רב הונא said.

keyTerms.meaning: חברים: people especially careful about the laws of purity
They purify, meaning they keep their food pure
Here too (applying the same idea to our case)

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא survives the challenge. The story of רבי could have involved the purity standards of קודש, so the רבנן's stricter view does not have to apply to תרומה.

phrases.english: It is like Ulla's statement,
for Ulla said:
The haverim keep things pure in the Galilee.
phrases.notes: He means they kept their food at the purity level used for קודש, even with no Temple.

phrases.english: Here too, in the days of Rebbi.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְעוּלָּא, דְּאָמַר עוּלָּא: חַבְרַיָּא מְדַכַּן בְּגָלִילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3 by showing that קודש-level purity did exist in רבי's time.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the story was about the purity standards of קודש, not תרומה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed there was no קודש-level purity in רבי's time, so the case had to be תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Some people kept the purity standards of קודש even then, so the case could have been about קודש, and רב הונא's ruling about תרומה stands.

steps.title: The story of רבן גמליאל's maidservant baking תרומה loaves
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells of a maidservant who baked תרומה loaves and found she was טמאה. רבן גמליאל first said all the loaves were impure. The case is about תרומה, which seems to contradict רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: There was a story with רבן גמליאל's maidservant. She was baking loaves of תרומה, and between each loaf she washed her hand and checked herself. After the last one she checked and found she was impure. She asked רבן גמליאל, and he said: 'They are all impure.' She said: 'רבי, didn't I check between every single one?' He said: 'If so, this last one is impure and all the rest are pure.' In any case, the ברייתא says 'loaves of תרומה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to challenge רב הונא again. In this story, רבן גמליאל treats the woman as impure backwards in time, and the food is תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said the רבנן's backdated impurity applies only to קודש, not to תרומה. Here רבן גמליאל's first ruling, 'they are all impure,' backdates her impurity onto earlier loaves, and the text explicitly says תרומה. Her checks between each loaf only limit how far back the impurity goes. The problem of backdating onto תרומה is still there.

keyTerms.meaning: Maidservant
Loaves of bread
A self-check for blood
Ritually impure (here, a נדה)
'In any case, it teaches': the גמרא points to the key detail in the source

steps.confusionAlert: רבן גמליאל's second ruling ('all the rest are pure') does not answer the question. Her checks only cut off the backdating. His first ruling still shows that backdating can apply to תרומה, and that is the problem for רב הונא.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
There was a story with the maidservant of רבן גמליאל
who was baking loaves of תרומה,
and between each and every one
she would rinse her hand in water and check herself.
After the last one she checked and found herself impure,
and she came and asked רבן גמליאל,
and he told her: They are all impure.
phrases.notes: He means all the loaves. Her impurity reaches back in time to the earlier loaves too.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה לוֹ: רַבִּי, וַהֲלֹא בְּדִיקָה הָיְתָה לִי
phrases.english: She said to him: My teacher, didn't I make a check
between each and every one!
He said to her: If so,
this one is impure and all the rest are pure.
In any case, it teaches: loaves of תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּשִׁפְחָתוֹ שֶׁל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the previous challenge to רב הונא was answered, the גמרא brings a new source to challenge him again.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that the רבנן's backdated impurity applies only to קודש, not to תרומה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבן גמליאל backdated the impurity onto loaves that the ברייתא explicitly calls תרומה.

steps.title: The 'תרומה' means the priest's share of the תודה loaves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads 'תרומה' as the priest's portion of the לחמי תודה, which counts as קודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: What 'תרומה' does it mean? The תרומה of the loaves of the thanks offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the word 'תרומה' in the story does not mean regular תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The loaves brought with a קרבן תודה include a portion given to the כהן, and the תורה also calls that portion 'תרומה.' Those loaves are קודש. So the story is about קודש, and רב הונא's rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The loaves brought along with a thanks offering
The share of those loaves given to the כהן; it is קודש, not regular תרומה

phrases.english: What is meant by 'תרומה'?
The תרומה of the loaves of the thanks offering.
phrases.notes: The תורה calls the כהן's share of these loaves 'תרומה' (ויקרא 7:14), even though they are holy offering food.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי תְּרוּמָה? תְּרוּמַת לַחְמֵי תוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word in the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'תרומה' means ordinary תרומה, so backdating applies to תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'תרומה' means the כהן's share of the לחמי תודה, which is קודש.

steps.title: Why would she bake the priest's share on its own?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the priest's share of the תודה loaves is normally taken only after baking, so why was she baking it separately?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the תרומה of the תודה loaves: what is it doing being baked?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own answer from step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally all the תודה loaves are baked together, and only afterward is one loaf of each kind given to the כהן. So no one bakes 'the תרומה of the לחמי תודה' as its own batch. The story says she baked תרומה loaves, so the new reading seems not to fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Baking
'What is it doing here?': this does not seem to fit

phrases.english: The תרומה of the thanks offering loaves:
what is it doing in the baking?
phrases.notes: The כהן's share is normally picked out only after all the loaves are baked.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּרוּמַת לַחְמֵי תוֹדָה בַּאֲפִיָּה מַאי בָּעֲיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading proposed in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of 'תרומה' as תרומת לחמי תודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That portion is set aside after baking, so it would never be baked as a separate group.

steps.title: They were set aside while still dough, as רב טובי taught
steps.stepSummary: The priest's share was set aside during kneading, before baking. The גמרא backs this up with רב טובי בר רב קטינא, who taught that baking just four loaves is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where they set them aside while kneading. This matches what רב טובי בר רב קטינא said: If one baked the תודה loaves as only four loaves, he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the priest's portion was separated while it was still dough, so it could be baked on its own. Then it brings a supporting teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the כהן's share is set aside at the kneading stage, it can be baked separately, and that fits the story. רב טובי's teaching about four loaves will show, in the next steps, why separating at kneading must sometimes happen.

keyTerms.meaning: He set them aside (as the כהן's portion)
Kneading (the dough stage)
Loaves or cakes
He has fulfilled his obligation

phrases.english: Where he set them aside while kneading them,

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי הָא דְּאָמַר רַב טוֹבִי בַּר רַב קַטִּינָא:
phrases.english: and like what רב טובי בר רב קטינא said:

phrases.aramaic: לַחְמֵי תוֹדָה שֶׁאֲפָאָן אַרְבַּע חַלּוֹת — יָצָא,
phrases.english: Thanks offering loaves that he baked as four loaves: he has fulfilled his obligation,
phrases.notes: That means one loaf of each of the four kinds, instead of the usual ten of each.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאַפְרְשִׁינְהוּ בְּלֵישַׁיְיהוּ, וְכִי הָא דְּאָמַר רַב טוֹבִי בַּר רַב קַטִּינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהן's share is always taken after baking.
steps.terutzMaskana: It can be set aside at the kneading stage and then baked separately.

steps.title: But forty loaves are required!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls an earlier discussion that questioned רב טובי: a תודה needs forty loaves, not four.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed it: But we need forty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא retells a discussion about רב טובי's teaching, starting with the question that was asked against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קרבן תודה comes with forty loaves, ten of each of four kinds. So how can four loaves be enough?

keyTerms.meaning: 'We discussed it': the גמרא recalls an earlier analysis
Forty (the full number of תודה loaves)

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
But we need forty!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָוֵינַן בַּהּ: וְהָא בָּעֵינַן אַרְבָּעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the supporting teaching quoted in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב טובי's teaching that four loaves are enough.

steps.title: Forty is only the best way
steps.stepSummary: Forty loaves are the ideal way to do the מצוה, but four are enough to fulfill the obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer: forty loaves are needed only to do the מצוה in the best way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forty loaves are the ideal, but they are not required. One loaf of each kind is enough to fulfill the obligation, so רב טובי's teaching stands.

keyTerms.meaning: As the ideal way to do the מצוה, but not required

phrases.english: For the ideal fulfillment of the מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 9.
steps.terutzMaskana: Forty is ideal; four is enough.

steps.title: With only four loaves, how is the priest's share taken?
steps.stepSummary: The כהן must get one loaf of each kind. Taking a slice from each of the four loaves is not allowed, because the תורה says 'one,' meaning a whole loaf.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we need to separate תרומה from them! And if you say he separates a slice from each one, the תורה said 'one,' meaning he may not take a slice.
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier discussion continues with a second problem with having only four loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With only four loaves, giving a whole loaf of each kind to the כהן would mean giving away all of them, which is not separating תרומה from them. Cutting a slice from each loaf does not work either, because the תורה requires a whole loaf ('one').

keyTerms.meaning: To separate or set aside
A slice or piece
'The Merciful One': the תורה

phrases.english: But we need to separate תרומה from them!
And if you would say that he separates a slice
from each and every one,
the תורה said 'one,'
meaning that he may not take a slice,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא בָּעֵינַן אַפְרוֹשֵׁי תְּרוּמָה מִינַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second problem with רב טובי's four-loaf teaching.
steps.kashyaTarget: How the כהן's share can be given when only four loaves are baked.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A whole loaf of each kind must go to the כהן, and a slice is not enough.

steps.title: Set aside at kneading, and the same in our story
steps.stepSummary: The answer was that the כהן's share was set aside at kneading. The same is true of the maidservant's loaves, so the story is about קודש and רב הונא stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we said that he set them aside at their kneading. Here too, they set them aside at their kneading.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes: just as in רב טובי's case the portion was set aside as dough, so too in the maidservant's story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Setting aside the כהן's share at the kneading stage is a real and accepted practice. So the maidservant could have been baking just that portion. Her loaves were קודש, and the challenge to רב הונא falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Here too': the same applies in our case

steps.whatToRemember: The 'תרומה' loaves in רבן גמליאל's story were the כהן's share of the לחמי תודה, set aside as dough. So they were קודש, and רב הונא's view, that backdated impurity applies only to קודש, still stands.

phrases.english: And we said that he set them aside while kneading them,
here too, they set them aside while kneading them.
phrases.notes: Back to the maidservant: her loaves were the כהן's share, set aside while still dough.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמְרִינַן דְּאַפְרְשִׁינְהוּ בְּלֵישַׁיְיהוּ, הָכָא נָמֵי דְּאַפְרְשִׁינְהוּ בְּלֵישַׁיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 and applies that answer back to the challenge in step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The maidservant's loaves were the כהן's share of the תודה, set aside at kneading, so they were קודש and רב הונא is not refuted.

steps.title: A second story about רבן גמליאל's maidservant
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another story. A maidservant checked herself between sealing each barrel of wine and found blood only after the last one. רבן גמליאל first said all the barrels were impure, then said only the last one was impure once he heard she had checked each time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: there was another story with רבן גמליאל's maidservant. She was sealing barrels of wine, and between each barrel she washed her hands and checked herself. After the last one she checked and found she was impure. She asked רבן גמליאל, and he said: 'They are all impure.' She said: 'But I checked between each one!' He said: 'If so, only this last one is impure and all the rest are pure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new story that it will use to challenge רב הונא. This step quotes the story; the actual difficulty comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל's first answer, 'all are impure,' is the 24-hour backward impurity of a נדה at work. Once she says she checked between each barrel, her clean checks cut the backward impurity short. The גמרא will now ask what this second story means for רב הונא, who limits מעת לעת to קודש.

keyTerms.meaning: Maidservant
Sealing barrels (closing them with a lid or plug)
A self-examination to check for menstrual blood
A 24-hour period; here, the 24 hours of backward impurity of a נדה

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: שׁוּב מַעֲשֶׂה בְּשִׁפְחָה שֶׁל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: Another story with the maidservant of רבן גמליאל,
who was sealing barrels of wine,
and between each and every one
she would rinse her hands in water and check herself,
and after the last one she checked and found she was impure,
and she came and asked רבן גמליאל,
and he said to her: They are all impure.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה לוֹ: וַהֲלֹא בְּדִיקָה הָיְתָה לִי
phrases.english: She said to him: But didn't I do a check
between each and every one!
He said to her: If so,
this one is impure and all the rest are pure.
phrases.notes: 'This one' means the last barrel, the one sealed after her last clean check.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: שׁוּב מַעֲשֶׂה בְּשִׁפְחָה שֶׁל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first maidservant story was settled as קודש, the גמרא brings a second story to test רב הונא again.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that מעת לעת applies only to קודש, not תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: a second, nearly identical question to רבן גמליאל suggests the two stories were about different kinds of food.

steps.title: Why would she ask the same question twice?
steps.stepSummary: If one story was about קודש and the other about תרומה, it makes sense that she came back to ask again. But if both were about קודש, why ask again? So the second story seems to be about תרומה, which goes against רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense if you say one story was about קודש and the other was about תרומה; that is why she came back and asked again. But if you say both were about קודש, why did she need to come back and ask?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the challenge. A second question only makes sense if the case was different, so the second story must be about תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the second story is about תרומה, then רבן גמליאל applied מעת לעת to תרומה. That contradicts רב הונא, who said מעת לעת is only for קודש. The extra visit to ask again is what the challenge rests on.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense if you say... (sets up the side that works)
This one and that one; both of them
The portion of produce given to a כהן; it has a lower level of holiness than קודש

phrases.english: It makes sense if you say
one was about קודש and one was about תרומה,
that is why she came back and asked again.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי דְּקֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: But if you say both were about קודש,
why did she need to come back and ask him?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא חֲדָא דְּקֹדֶשׁ, וַחֲדָא דִּתְרוּמָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the story from step 13 into a direct challenge against רב הונא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא: מעת לעת applies only to קודש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second question suggests a different case. Since the first story was about קודש, the second must be תרומה, and רבן גמליאל applied מעת לעת to it.

steps.title: It was two different maidservants
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that both stories were about קודש. Two different maidservants each asked their own question, so no one asked twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: The story that happened happened with two different maidservants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Different women asked, so the second question does not show the case was different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the same woman came back to ask the same thing. If the questions came from two different maidservants, each one simply asked about her own case. Both stories can be about קודש, so רב הונא stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The story that happened
Two maidservants

steps.whatToRemember: In the first version, רב הונא limits מעת לעת to קודש. Both maidservant stories are explained as קודש, so his view survives.

phrases.english: The story that happened —
happened with two maidservants.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁהָיָה בִּשְׁתֵּי שְׁפָחוֹת הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: two different people, not one person asking twice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The same maidservant came back, so the second case must have been different (תרומה).
steps.terutzMaskana: Two maidservants each asked about קודש, so רב הונא is not disproven.

steps.title: Another version of רב הונא's ruling
steps.stepSummary: Some report רב הונא differently: the 24-hour backward impurity of a נדה applies to both קודש and תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it in another version. רב הונא said: the 24-hour backward impurity of a נדה makes things impure, both קודש and תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts over with a different report of what רב הונא said. In this version he says the opposite: מעת לעת applies to תרומה too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רב הונא limited מעת לעת to קודש. In this version, it covers תרומה as well. The next few steps (17-19) discuss this second version.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version of the statement
A woman who has seen menstrual blood
Makes things impure

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions! Version one: only קודש. Version two (here): both קודש and תרומה.

phrases.english: Some say it in another version,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: מֵעֵת לְעֵת שֶׁבְּנִדָּה
phrases.english: רב הונא said: the 24-hour period of a נדה
makes impure both קודש and תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִישָּׁנָא אַחֲרִינָא אָמְרִי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second report of רב הונא's ruling, which reverses the first one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מעת לעת of a נדה makes both קודש and תרומה impure.

steps.title: Proof: it is not on the list of extra stringencies
steps.stepSummary: The source for רב הונא is that the משנה listing the extra stringencies of קודש over תרומה does not include מעת לעת. So מעת לעת applies to תרומה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this? From the fact that it is not taught in the list of extra stringencies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רב הונא's source and gives it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a משנה listing the extra purity rules that apply only to קודש and not to תרומה. If מעת לעת were only for קודש, it would be on that list. Since it is missing, it must apply to תרומה as well.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?
Extra stringencies of purity that apply to קודש but not to תרומה

phrases.english: From where do we know this?
Since it is not taught together with the list of stringencies.
phrases.notes: This is the list in the משנה in חגיגה of strict rules for קודש that do not apply to תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? מִדְּלָא קָתָנֵי לַהּ גַּבֵּי מַעֲלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the ruling in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: מעת לעת applies to תרומה as well as קודש
steps.raayaSupportSource: Its absence from the list of מעלות in the משנה in חגיגה

steps.title: רב נחמן: a ברייתא says not for תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן points to a ברייתא that says outright that מעת לעת applies to קודש but not to תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: But a תנא teaches: for קודש, but not for תרומה!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן challenges רב הונא's second version with a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא learned his rule from a silence, the missing item on the list. רב נחמן brings a ברייתא that openly says מעת לעת does not apply to תרומה. A clear statement in a ברייתא outweighs a proof from silence.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage of the משנה period; here, the teacher of a ברייתא
But isn't it so that... (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: רב נחמן said to him:
But a תנא teaches:
For קודש, but not for תרומה!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן: וְהָא תָּנֵי תַּנָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second version of רב הונא given in steps 16-17.
steps.kashyaTarget: Second version of רב הונא: מעת לעת applies to תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא openly limits מעת לעת to קודש and excludes תרומה.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about חולין kept at different purity levels
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק explains the ברייתא. It means חולין prepared at the purity level of קודש are affected, while חולין prepared at the purity level of תרומה are not. תרומה itself is still affected, so רב הונא stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק accepted it from him and explained: the ברייתא means חולין prepared with the purity of קודש, but not חולין prepared with the purity of תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is reread so it no longer contradicts רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'קודש' and 'תרומה' in the ברייתא do not mean real קודש and real תרומה. They refer to ordinary food (חולין) handled at those purity levels. Real תרומה is still made impure by מעת לעת, just as רב הונא said.

keyTerms.meaning: He accepted it from him (and explained it)
Ordinary food that is not holy
Kept at the purity standard of קודש

steps.whatToRemember: In the second version, רב הונא holds that מעת לעת applies to both קודש and תרומה. The ברייתא that seems to exclude תרומה is only talking about חולין kept at the purity level of תרומה.

phrases.aramaic: קַבְּלַהּ מִינֵּיהּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק accepted it from him:
phrases.notes: He means: he took רב נחמן's ברייתא and explained what it really means.

phrases.english: It applies to חולין prepared with the purity of קודש,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא בְּחוּלִּין שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ עַל טׇהֳרַת תְּרוּמָה.
phrases.english: but not to חולין prepared with the purity of תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַבְּלַהּ מִינֵּיהּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's challenge from step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the ברייתא: its terms refer to חולין handled at those purity levels
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא excludes real תרומה from מעת לעת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא excludes only חולין kept at the purity level of תרומה; real תרומה is affected, so רב הונא stands.

steps.title: A משנה about dough that may have become impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: if a doubt of impurity arose about dough before kneading, it may be prepared in impurity. If the doubt arose after kneading, it must be prepared in purity.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: if a doubt arose whether a dough became impure, then before it was kneaded it may be prepared in impurity, and after it was kneaded it must be prepared in purity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings in a new source, a משנה from מסכת חלה, about dough that may have become impure. The next step will explain the reasoning behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה draws a line at the moment of kneading. Before kneading, there is no need to protect the dough from impurity. After kneading, the dough must be protected. The משנה gives the rule without the reason, and the גמרא supplies the reason next.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt whether something became impure
She (the dough) was kneaded or rolled
It may be prepared in impurity, even with impure hands or vessels
It must be prepared in purity

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: "There" means a משנה in another מסכתא, here מסכת חלה.

phrases.english: If a doubt of impurity arose regarding it,
phrases.notes: "It" is a dough, which is a feminine word in Hebrew.

phrases.english: before it was kneaded
it may be prepared in impurity;
after it was kneaded
it must be prepared in purity.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 19 discussed חולין that are prepared at a higher purity level, the גמרא brings a related משנה about ordinary dough that must sometimes be guarded in purity.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dough with a doubt of impurity may be prepared in impurity before kneading. After kneading, it must be prepared in purity.

steps.title: Why kneading changes the rule: kneaded dough is treated like חלה
steps.stepSummary: Before kneading, the dough is plain חולין, and it is allowed to make חולין impure. After kneading, it is dough from which חלה has not yet been separated. That dough counts like חלה, and חלה may not be made impure. The step ends by opening a new ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Before it was kneaded, it may be prepared in impurity, because it is ordinary food, and it is allowed to make ordinary food impure in ארץ ישראל. After it was kneaded, it must be prepared in purity, because ordinary dough that still needs חלה separated is considered like חלה, and it is forbidden to make חלה impure. A ברייתא taught:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind each half of the משנה. At the very end, the word תָּנָא opens a new ברייתא, whose content comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Kneading is what makes dough obligated in חלה. Before that point, the dough is simply חולין, and making חולין impure is allowed. Once kneaded, the dough still contains the חלה that has not been separated yet, so the whole dough is treated like חלה and must be kept pure.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary, non-holy food
To cause something to become impure
Food from which חלה has not yet been separated
The portion of dough given to a כהן, which is holy like תרומה

steps.confusionAlert: The kneaded dough has not turned into חלה. It is still חולין. It is only treated like חלה for this rule, because the חלה portion inside it has not yet been separated.
steps.whatToRemember: Before kneading, dough is plain חולין and may be made impure. After kneading, it is treated like חלה and must be kept pure.

phrases.english: Before it was kneaded
it may be prepared in impurity,
because it is ordinary food,
and it is permitted to cause impurity
to ordinary food in the Land of Israel;
after it was kneaded
it must be prepared in purity,
because ordinary food that still needs חלה separated
is considered like חלה itself,
and it is forbidden to cause impurity to חלה.
A ברייתא taught:

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד שֶׁלֹּא גִּלְגְּלָהּ תֵּעָשֶׂה בְּטוּמְאָה חוּלִּין נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind both halves of the משנה quoted in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before kneading, dough is חולין and may be made impure. After kneading, dough from which חלה has not been separated is treated like חלה and may not be made impure.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that ordinary food can be treated with a higher level of holiness when a holy portion is still mixed inside it.
